motivation: FIRST case in the dataset whose BREAK was NOT sourced from BUMP. The break was discovered by mine_advisories.py from the OSV Maven security-advisory feed (CVE-2022-1471), and real client adaptations were found via GitHub commit search (bbc_e2e.py mine-commits). Proves the external-mining pipeline yields verifiable production BBC cases beyond BUMP's ~8 semantic breaks.

in_repo_version_transition_AUDIT.finding: The behavioural MECHANISM (snakeyaml 1.x permissive -> 2.0 default-deny) is verified via the harness across a 1.33->2.0 swap. However the real clients did NOT traverse the 1.x->2.0 boundary IN-REPO — they responded to snakeyaml 2.x's default-deny BEHAVIOUR while already on 2.x. So these are genuine (behaviour -> production re-permit adaptation) pairs, but NOT witnessed (version-bump -> break -> fix) traversals like the BUMP-sourced xstream cases (where BUMP pins the exact breaking dependency-bump commit).
in_repo_version_transition_AUDIT.mongoose-plugins: snakeyaml resolved to 2.4 at BOTH parent (3189305106) and adapt (9e5916e1) commit (transitive via com.telamin:mongoose:1.0.17); adapt commit touches no pom. No 1.x->2.0 bump — repo was already on 2.4, fixed FQN-loading against the 2.x default. Confirmed via mvn dependency:tree.
in_repo_version_transition_AUDIT.KartaEmeraldCurrency: snakeyaml is NOT pinned in-repo — provided transitively by the Paper server runtime (compileOnly io.papermc.paper:paper-api); adapt commit touches no build file. Commit body explicitly: 'ComposerException ... caused by recent versions of SnakeYAML disallowing deserialization of arbitrary Java objects by default'. Response to 2.x runtime behaviour, no in-repo version transition.
in_repo_version_transition_AUDIT.quarkus: NOT a break response — proactive hardening (new Yaml() -> new SafeConstructor()) on its own trusted plain-map extension YAML, which never failed under 2.0. Caught by the noisy 'SafeConstructor' search term.

external_source.discovered_via: mine_advisories.py (OSV Maven feed) -> deserialize tier, default-deny

behavioral_break.exception: org.yaml.snakeyaml.error.YAMLException: Global tag is not allowed: tag:yaml.org,2002:com.example.MyNode
behavioral_break.affected_class: com.example.MyNode (a type referenced from YAML by FQN global tag)
behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: snakeyaml 2.0 (CVE-2022-1471) makes SafeConstructor / a restrictive LoaderOptions TagInspector the default: `new Yaml().loadAs(...)` no longer instantiates arbitrary Java types from YAML global tags. YAML mapping to application types that 1.x deserialized now throws at load time. Code compiles; it throws at runtime on previously-accepted input -> behavioural break. NOTE: 2.0 ALSO ships a separate COMPILE break (Constructor now requires a LoaderOptions arg); the differential's parent uses plain `new Yaml()` to isolate the behavioural break from that.

adaptation.summary: Re-permit the client's own types under 2.0's default-deny by installing a TagInspector on LoaderOptions. Direct YAML analogue of xstream's allowTypes(...) allowlist.

real_clients_signature_confirmed.why_not_run_directly: break site is a private method wired into runtime Fluxtion graph compilation; repo targets Java 21 with snakeyaml transitive via a SNAPSHOT reactor -> not cheaply runnable, so recorded signature_confirmed (cf. POI).

verification.method: 3-state differential build+test with Maven on JDK 11; snakeyaml version swapped via -Dsnakeyaml.version; parent vs adapted code selected via Maven profile (-Pparent / -Padapted) because the adapted variant uses the 2.0-only setTagInspector API.

verification.conclusion: Confirmed behavioural break with a production-side adaptation: a passing YAML load breaks only under snakeyaml >=2.0 with otherwise-unchanged code, and installing a TagInspector on LoaderOptions in production code resolves it. The break + adaptation pattern is taken verbatim from the real signature_confirmed clients above.
